Yes, the melt() function in the reshape2 package will do the trick.

## I think this what your data look like:
test <- data.frame(Time = 1:20, Sta1 = rnorm(20), Sta2 = rnorm(20), Sta3 = rnorm(20))

head(test)

1    1 -0.849412015  1.11316981  0.9303466
2    2 -0.943124251  2.41267782  0.1310218
3    3 -1.134935071 -0.27169808 -0.7537679
4    4 -0.369759824  1.89524403  0.6356290

## check out ?melt for more info
testm <- melt(test, id.vars = 'Time')
head(testm)

2     2     Sta1 -0.943124251
3     3     Sta1 -1.134935071
4     4     Sta1 -0.369759824
5     5     Sta1  0.721777055
6     6     Sta1 -0.006843206
- Patrick

messages.subject: manipulation of lists
messages.body_plain:
I'm working on a problem which is exposing my ignorance of how to manipulate lists. I have a list of lists, where the first list is a set of candidate specific lists. Within each candidate's list, the first element is a data frame consisting of biographical data, and the subsequent elements are data frames consisting of group ratings of the candidate.

An indicative example is provided below

library(plyr)

df1.l<- rlply(3, data.frame(cand = sample(letters, 1),
                            y.start = sample(1980:1990, 1),
                            y.end = sample(1991:2012, 1)))
df2.l<- rlply(9, data.frame(group = rep(c(paste(sample(letters, size=4, replace = T), sep = "")), times = 4),
                            year = sample(1990:2012, size = 4),
                            score = runif(4,0,1)))

a <- list(df1.l[[1]],df2.l[[1]], df2.l[[2]],df2.l[[3]])
b <- list(df1.l[[2]],df2.l[[4]], df2.l[[5]],df2.l[[6]])
d <- list(df1.l[[3]],df2.l[[7]], df2.l[[8]],df2.l[[9]])

biglist <- list(a,b,d)

Ideally, I want a data frame, where every candidate's biographical details are appended to their group assessments. That is, each candidate's data frames will be bound by rows, and then this frame will be column bound with the candidate's biographical details.

For instance, the element biglist[[1]] will eventually become

  cand y.start y.end  group year     score
1    m    1989  2004  g     1993 0.9033009
2    m    1989  2004  l     1995 0.7066574
3    m    1989  2004  q     2004 0.1573602

what complicates things is that the ratings data frame within each candidate element are heterogeneous in two ways--there are a changing number of these frames, and each rating frame is itself possessed of a different number of rows.

I tried to use an llply call to split biglist into candidate specific lists, and then use an ldply call within this function to bind the data frames my required way, but I got nowhere.

Any assistance you can provide will be hugely appreciated!

> I'm working on a problem which is exposing my ignorance of how to
> manipulate lists. I have a list of lists, where the first list is a set of
> candidate specific lists. Within each candidate's list, the first element
> is a data frame consisting of biographical data, and the subsequent
> elements are data frames consisting of group ratings of the candidate.
>
> An indicative example is provided below
>
> library(plyr)
>
> df1.l<- rlply(3, data.frame(cand = sample(letters, 1),
>                              y.start = sample(1980:1990, 1),
>                              y.end = sample(1991:2012, 1)))
> df2.l<- rlply(9, data.frame(group = rep(c(paste(sample(letters, size=4,
> replace = T), sep = "")), times = 4),
>                              year = sample(1990:2012, size = 4),
>                              score = runif(4,0,1)))
>
> a<- list(df1.l[[1]],df2.l[[1]], df2.l[[2]],df2.l[[3]])
> b<- list(df1.l[[2]],df2.l[[4]], df2.l[[5]],df2.l[[6]])
> d<- list(df1.l[[3]],df2.l[[7]], df2.l[[8]],df2.l[[9]])
>
> biglist<- list(a,b,d)
>
> Ideally, I want a data frame, where every candidate's biographical details
> are appended to their group assessments. That is, each candidate's data
> frames will be bound by rows, and then this frame will be column bound with
> the candidate's biographical details.
>
> For instance, the element biglist[[1]] will eventually become
>
>    cand y.start y.end  group year     score
> 1    m    1989  2004  g     1993 0.9033009
>
> 2    m    1989  2004  l     1995 0.7066574
>
> 3    m    1989  2004  q     2004 0.1573602
>
>
>
> what complicates things is that the ratings data frame within each
> candidate element are heterogeneous in two ways--there are a changing
> number of these frames, and each rating frame is itself possessed of
> a different number of rows.
>
> I tried to use an llply call to split biglist into candidate specific
> lists, and then use an ldply call within this function to bind the
> data frames my required way, but I got nowhere.
>
> Any assistance you can provide will be hugely appreciated!

Does this give you what you want?

llply(biglist, function(l) {cbind(l[1], do.call(rbind, l[-1]))})

I'm only using llply to iterate through the list of candidates. The
binding of dataframes (rbinding all but the first, cbinding the first to
that) is just a single function.  I could replace the do.call(rbind...)
part with another plyr call

llply(biglist, function(l) {cbind(l[1], ldply(l[-1], identity))})

Both these approaches will handle the heterogeneities you describe; the
latter will also handle the columns of group assessment data.frames
being different (with NA's filling in where columns don't exist).

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Is there a counterpart of the aggregate like this using ddply?

> aggregate(.~Species, data=iris, FUN=mean)
     Species Sepal.Length Sepal.Width Petal.Length Petal.Width
1     setosa        5.006       3.428        1.462       0.246
2 versicolor        5.936       2.770        4.260       1.326
3  virginica        6.588       2.974        5.552       2.026

I know
> ddply(iris, .(Species), summarize, Sepal.Length = mean(Sepal.Length))
but the "." indicating "anything else" is useful especially when the
data.frame contains only one categorical variable and many continuous
variable.

thanks in advance,

kohske

messages.subject: Using melt on table objects
messages.body_plain:
I used melt on a table object and expected it to work the same as for matrices, but it doesn't. With matrices, it will use the names of the dimensions as column headers, but it doesn't seem to do the same thing for a table, even though the data structures are very similar.

m <- matrix(101:106, nrow=2, dimnames=list(therows=1:2, thecols=1:3))
#        thecols
# therows   1   2   3
#       1 101 103 105
#       2 102 104 106

# It's an array
is.array(m)
# TRUE

# This automatically sets column names to 'therows' and 'thecols'
melt(m)
# therows thecols value
#       1       1   101
#       2       1   102
#       1       2   103
#       2       2   104
#       1       3   105
#       2       3   106

# Convert it to a table
t <- as.table(m)

# The table object is an array
is.array(t)
# TRUE

# Structures are very similar
str(m)
# int [1:2, 1:3] 101 102 103 104 105 106
# - attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
#  ..$ therows: chr [1:2] "1" "2"
#  ..$ thecols: chr [1:3] "1" "2" "3"
str(t)
# 'table' int [1:2, 1:3] 101 102 103 104 105 106
# - attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
#  ..$ therows: chr [1:2] "1" "2"
#  ..$ thecols: chr [1:3] "1" "2" "3"

# Melted table has strange column names
melt(t)
# value NA  NA
#     1  1 101
#     2  1 102
#     1  2 103
#     2  2 104
#     1  3 105
#     2  3 106

Is this the expected behavior? It seems odd to me.

-Winston
